title: Potassium & the ECG

findings.where: potassium.jsx — dynamicCaption(), K_EXTREME.hi; worked step for values such as k = 8.4
findings.title: Severe hyperkalemia receives borderline-result urgency language
findings.problem: For potassium values through 9.5 mEq/L, the hyperkalemia branch provides no explicit urgent-assessment or escalation statement. An 8.4 result receives the same generic 'urgency depends ... not on the number alone' wording as 5.01. Severe hyperkalemia warrants emergency assessment even without symptoms or ECG changes; the arbitrary >9.5 extreme-value trigger misses this.
findings.fix: Add a separate severe-hyperkalemia branch using a cited reference threshold—commonly ≥6.5 mEq/L, with protocol variation acknowledged. Explicitly teach urgent assessment, cardiac monitoring and escalation even with a normal ECG. Reserve the generic context-dependent urgency wording for less severe elevations.

findings.where: Images 1, 6, 8 and 13 — hyperkalemia care panel; hyper-care caption and narration; GOALS and Frame description
findings.title: The treatment explanation omits repeat potassium assessment
findings.problem: Claim 10 includes potassium reassessment, but none of the learner-facing treatment explanations carries it through. They emphasize glucose monitoring after insulin while omitting reassessment of potassium itself. Because intracellular shifting is temporary, learners need to understand that the response must be checked and rebound hyperkalemia can occur.
findings.fix: Add prescribed repeat serum-potassium assessment and rebound surveillance to the care panel, caption, narration and accessible description. Keep this as an exam-prep monitoring principle without supplying treatment doses or monitoring intervals.

assessment: Do not publish: the worked-example logic under-triages severe hyperkalemia, and an important monitoring safeguard appears only in the facts list.
